newsitem.title: USA: Paracelsus Healthcare sued in class action.
newsitem.headline: Paracelsus Healthcare sued in class action.

text.p: A purported class action lawsuit has been filed against Paracelsus Healthcare Corp, accusing the company of using misleading and false statements that inflated the price of its stock, lawyers for the plaintiffs said on Friday.
The suit alleges that the inflated stock price led to the merger of Champion Healthcare Corp into Paracelsus, the law firm Bernstein Litowitz Berger & Grossman LLP said.
Paracelsus acquired Champion for about 19.8 million shares in August.
Paracelsus could not be reached for comment on the suit, filed in District Court in Harris County, Texas. The plaintiffs were not identified.
The suit alleges that Paracelsus "misrepresented its financial condition" in documents related to its quarters ended December 31, 1995, March 31, 1996, and June 30, 1996.
It also alleges that Paracelsus had "serious flaws in its internal accounting and financial reporting system and controls."

Earlier this week Paracelsus requested that the New York Stock Exchange halt trading of its shares. On Wednesday it said its third quarter earnings would fall well short of expectations, and it might have to restate its financial results for the 1995 fourth quarter and the 1996 first and second quarters.
Paracelsus's stock closed Wednesday at 10-1/8. This morning it stood at 5-1/8.
